sections.label: A conversation analogy
sections.intro: We both understand because we agree on rules:
rules: take turns in the right order (order)
ask for a repeat if not understood (error handling)

sections.text: Protocols let independent devices interpret the same exchange.

layers.name: Link
layers.text: local delivery on a network (e.g. Ethernet)

layers.name: Physical
layers.text: bits over a medium (wires, radio, fibre)

items.heading: Syntax
items.text: Format of the data. E.g. message fields, headers, character encoding.

items.heading: Meaning
items.text: What the data represents. E.g. `GET` means "request a web page".

items.heading: Order
items.text: Steps must happen in a specific sequence. E.g. connect before sending data.

items.heading: Error handling
items.text: Detect problems and recover. E.g. checksums, timeouts, retransmission, error messages.

items.heading: Ethernet
items.text: Moves frames on a local network.

items.heading: IP
items.text: Addresses packets and helps route them between networks.

items.heading: TCP
items.text: Reliable, ordered delivery with error handling (e.g. retransmits lost data).

items.heading: UDP
items.text: Simple, best-effort delivery. No guarantee of delivery, ordering or recovery.

items.heading: DNS
items.text: Translates names (e.g. example.com) to IP addresses.

items.heading: HTTP
items.text: Transfers web content between browsers and web servers.

sections.text: Protocols are agreements. Without them, devices could not understand each other.
